title: Question 5
stem:
A stationary loudspeaker emits sound of constant frequency. A microphone is placed near to the loudspeaker and connected to a cathode-ray oscilloscope (CRO). The trace on the screen of the CRO is shown in Fig. 5.1.

{{figure:figure_5_1}}

Fig. 5.1

The time-base of the CRO is set to $5.0 \times 10^{-4} \text{s cm}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
The speed of the sound emitted by the loudspeaker is $330 \text{m s}^{-1}$.

Determine the wavelength of the sound.
hints: Hint 1: Look along the horizontal time axis of Fig. 5.1. Find one complete oscillation, for example from one peak to the next peak, and estimate how many cm that covers.
Hint 2: Use the time-base setting to turn that horizontal length in cm into a real time. What does that time represent for the sound wave?
Hint 3: You now know the wave speed $v$ and the period $T$. Recall how $v$, frequency $f$ and wavelength $\lambda$ are linked, with $f = 1/T$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Reading One Period from the CRO Trace**
You are sitting with the CRO picture. The horizontal direction is time, the vertical is the sound signal. One full wave means peak to the next identical peak. Counting the small 1 cm squares in Fig. 5.1, that distance is about $5.8\text{ cm}$. A common slip is to count amplitude vertically - for period you must stay horizontal.

Step 2: **Turning cm into Seconds**
The time-base tells you what each cm means: $5.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ s cm}^{-1}$. So multiply:
$$T = 5.8 \times 5.0 \times 10^{-4}$$
$$T = 2.9 \times 10^{-3}\text{ s}$$
This is the true period of the sound wave, about $2.9\text{ ms}$.

Step 3: **Using Wave Speed to Get Wavelength**
For any progressive wave the speed, frequency and wavelength are linked by:
$$v = f\lambda \text{ with } f = \frac{1}{T}$$
So it is convenient to use $\lambda = vT$:
$$\lambda = 330 \times 2.9 \times 10^{-3}$$
$$\lambda = 0.96\text{ m}$$
That is just under one metre, sensible for a few-hundred-hertz sound in air.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The loudspeaker now moves in a straight line while emitting the same sound of constant frequency. The period of the trace on the CRO increases continuously.

Describe the motion of the loudspeaker.

markscheme_points.text: at an increasing speed / whilst accelerating

hints: Hint 1: The CRO period is the observed period at the microphone. If that period gets longer, what is happening to the observed frequency?
Hint 2: Recall the Doppler effect for sound. Which direction of source motion gives a lower observed frequency, and what does a continuously changing shift tell you about the speed?
parts.proper_answer: The loudspeaker moves away from the microphone, with increasing speed - it is accelerating away.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **What a Longer Period Means**
The microphone and CRO detect the wave as it arrives. A larger period $T_{obs}$ means a smaller observed frequency, since $f_{obs} = 1/T_{obs}$. The source still emits the same true frequency, so the change must be due to motion - this is the Doppler effect.

Step 2: **Away and Speeding Up**
When a source moves away from a stationary observer, the wavefronts are stretched out behind it, so the observed wavelength is longer and the observed frequency is lower. That explains the increase in period. Because the period increases continuously, the Doppler shift is getting bigger all the time. So the recession speed is not constant, it is increasing. In short, the loudspeaker is accelerating away from the microphone in a straight line.
